applies_why: Yes, the judge text resolves the D5/C5 collision by isolated verse and word observations rather than by chain-against-chain footing.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse.' Reading 1: compare the two whole chains by their support. Reading 2: compare individual verses or words within the collision. I used Reading 1.
why: Because the judge text decides the D5/C5 collision by noting particular Isaiah bounds, a single Matthew 1:23 concession, and almah/bethulah word count, it weighs verse by verse rather than chain against chain by footing as K-C requires.
